title: ‘Hockey Night in Canada: Punjabi Edition’ ends after 18-year television run
content:
“Hockey Night in Canada: Punjabi Edition” has been cancelled after an 18-year run, the program announced on its X account. A spinoff show of “Hockey Night in Canada,” the television program broadcast NHL games in Punjabi on Saturday nights. The broadcasts were available on OMNI Television, a multilingual, free, over-the-air channel based in Canada.

The show featured several South Asian broadcasters and presenters, including Harnarayan Singh, who went viral for his call of Pittsburgh Penguins forward Nick Bonino’s winning goal in Game 1 of the 2016 Stanley Cup Final against the San Jose Sharks. The broadcast also featured host Randip Janda, who also worked with Sportsnet on Vancouver Canucks game broadcasts as the first full-time radio commentator of South Asian descent in NHL history.

“For 18 years, this show brought our community closer to the game we love,” the program’s statement read. “It shared the stories of South Asian players and families and created a space that was truly unique in Canadian sports. We are incredibly proud of what we built together.”

The news comes after it was announced in June that “Hockey Night in Canada” would be coming off the air after 74 years. The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation and Rogers Communications did not renew their 12-year sublicensing agreement, which allowed “Hockey Night in Canada” to be broadcast on Rogers channels, including Sportsnet. Rogers is about to begin a new 12-year national broadcasting deal to air NHL games this fall, with Amazon Prime Video airing Wednesday night games and select Stanley Cup playoff games next spring.

The CBC still owns the rights to “Hockey Night in Canada” and plans to use the brand in “different ways going forward,” CBC head of public affairs Chuck Thompson told The Athletic in June.

This story will be updated.
